reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: A gate unmet for four sessions is a hypothesis about the OWNER, and it was never tested. The probe harness gating all of Phase 1 had never once been exercised. Driving it took one session and found a bug that leaks the bank plus a framing trap that would have produced the wrong ruling. When a blocker is waiting on a human, check the thing you would be handing them FIRST.

The probe is solo-only by construction; B3/B4 are six-seat claims. Solo receives the whole arena faucet, so it fills an 8-slot bank 6x faster than the condition being ruled on. Correct code, correct measurements, wrong CONDITION -- and nothing in the harness said so. Ask what the instrument is a measurement OF, not only whether it measures accurately.

Re-learned the hard way from this repo own boot snapshot. I called lambda*W wrong in both directions from a 63s window on a 10s-TTL process and a 12s run held entirely inside the ramp. Both readings were artifacts of my protocol, not the instrument. A tick-locked census past the ramp showed the model exact: throughput 0.1933 vs 0.1875, lifetime 600/600/600.

Two defects in my own change survived 2001 passing tests and were caught by screenshotting the overlay: max-width:44ch clipping every long line (including content shipped in S128), and a ramp threshold in the wrong units that demanded 360s while promising 60s. Every string was CORRECT; the viewport and the denominator were wrong. Render the thing.

The one-line reorder fixing the consume-before-refuse bug was untestable: the live handler is unreachable from vitest, and a source-order assertion is a known trap here because indexOf matches your own comments -- and my new comment named shift four times. Moving decision+consume into one unit that owns the array made the bug class observable from Node instead of pinned by prose.

A recursive grep of dist/ said PROBE_SENTINEL leaked into production. It had not -- the only hit was a sourcemap sourcesContent, and the documented contract is dist/assets/*.js specifically. I nearly reported a leak that was not there. Sixth consecutive session where verify-the-reviewer-MECHANISM applied, and this time the reviewer was me.

Q IS double-bound between the probe draw and SHRINK_TERRITORY. It cannot fire only because decideKeyShrink returns false in solo and the probe is solo-only -- an unrelated guard is the sole thing preventing it. Refuted as a present defect, logged as a carry-forward, because the reason it is safe is not the reason anyone would assume.

calibration.tier_accuracy: PDR declared Micro (<10K, 1 code file + 2 doc files). Actual: 1 code file + 1 test file + 2 doc files + plan/state bookkeeping. Micro was the RIGHT call on token cost and blast radius -- the whole change is DEV-only and cannot reach production -- but the file count ran over the Micro guideline of 1-2 because the fix needed its own test file edit and two docs carry the recipe the owner reads. Recording it as a borderline Micro rather than pretending it fit: no tier escalation was warranted, since escalating to Standard would have bought a 3-way Council on a 3-line reorder in a file that ships zero bytes.
calibration.estimate_vs_actual: Predicted 'the shift-before-guard bug, an on-overlay seat-share caveat, and a corrected playtest recipe'. All three landed. UNPREDICTED and larger than any of them: the change itself contained two defects (44ch clipping, ramp threshold in the wrong units) that 2001 passing tests could not see, plus a pre-existing S128 clipping defect the widening incidentally fixed. Estimating 'small fix' was right about the code and wrong about the verification cost -- the screenshot pass found more than the reducer pass did.
calibration.a0_value: A.0 was the entire session. The scoped work (a 3-line reorder) would have been worthless without it: the reason to touch this file at all came from driving the instrument, and the highest-value finding -- DELTA-1, the solo-vs-6-seat trap -- is not a code defect at all and no amount of reading would have produced it. what_worked: Testing the INSTRUMENT before asking the human a fifth time. Four sessions had recorded the probe playtest as blocked on the owner; nobody had checked what would be handed to them. One session of driving it found a bank-draining bug and a framing trap that would have produced the wrong ruling on seven Full-tier slots.

Reading the boot snapshot's CRITICAL TRAPS as a live checklist rather than history. 'A blocked verification path usually has a side door one layer over' is precisely why the DOM overlay turned out to need no compositing at all -- two prior sessions had recorded HUD verification as impossible, and that constraint simply did not apply.

Restructuring so the bug class became testable instead of pinning it with prose. The reorder alone was unverifiable from vitest, and a source-order assertion was a known trap here -- my own new comment named `shift` four times and would have blinded it. Moving decision+consume into one unit that owns the array made 'consumed despite refusing' directly observable from Node.

Mutation-testing every assertion, 8 for 8, including a mutation that re-introduces the exact original bug. S131 broke 4 of its own 4 new guards this way; treating that as a standing requirement rather than a war story is what made these guards real.
Screenshotting the result. It found two defects in my own change that the full green suite structurally could not -- every string was correct; the viewport and the denominator were wrong.

Measuring throughput and per-spark lifetime instead of the standing pool. The pool is a consequence; throughput is the constraint that governs bank-fill time. That reframe is what turned two contradictory pool readings into a clean confirmation of B3.
what_i_got_wrong: Called lambda*W 'wrong in both directions' from a 63s window on a 10s-TTL process and a 12s run held entirely inside the ramp. Both were artifacts of my reading protocol. The boot snapshot already carried #measure-inside-the-hold-not-on-the-edge-of-the-ramp from S131 and I walked into it anyway -- reading a lesson is not the same as having it.

Shipped a ramp warning whose threshold was in the wrong units (poolSamples.length vs sim ticks), so it demanded 360s while its own message promised 60s. I wrote a warning ABOUT sampling timescales and got the sampling timescale wrong inside it.

Reported a production LEAK from a recursive grep of dist/ when the only hit was a sourcemap's sourcesContent and the documented contract is dist/assets/*.js. Nearly escalated a non-defect; caught it by checking the mechanism.

Widened `git add -A .claude/` and swept in `.claude/session-state.s129.bak`, an untracked leftover that was not in the PDR's scope. Disclosed to the owner rather than left for them to find in a diff, but the right move was a narrower add.

Lost two tool calls to the project's own documented traps -- a heredoc mangled by apostrophes, and a `sed`/`grep` anchor that missed because the PDR's status line is bold markdown (`**STATUS: ...**`) rather than bare. Both were written down; I did not consult them until after they bit.

unverified_at_close: The playtest itself -- B4 is a human judgment about whether carving survives an 8-slot exact-type inventory, and no headless run substitutes for it. STILL THE PHASE-1 GATE.
deploy.yml has STILL never executed with S131's CI gate -- no write auth, 35 commits unpushed. Static assertions only. Unchanged from S131 and now one session older.

The corrected `&spawn=0.03125` recipe is verified to RENDER correctly and to be accepted by `seatShareReadout`, but no one has yet played a full match under it. The supply arithmetic is confirmed; the resulting play experience is not.

`fillFairShareSec` is an equal-split idealisation. Real 6-seat contention was never measured -- the probe cannot measure it, being solo-only. Correct for ruling on aggregate supply, wrong for predicting any individual seat, and labelled as such on screen.

The Q double-binding is refuted as a PRESENT defect but not structurally prevented. It is held off only by `decideKeyShrink` returning false in solo plus the probe's solo-only auto-disarm -- an incidental guard, not a deliberate one.

Sourcemaps in `dist/` embed the full TypeScript of every DEV-only module including this harness. Not a code leak (the executable is clean, 0 probe identifiers), but whether `.map` files are actually deployed was NOT investigated this session.
